capabilities: display the heading tree of the current content while editing or reading
click sticky headings to scroll to the corresponding section
toggle between default mode (with siblings) and concise mode (current heading plus ancestors)
work in editing mode, reading mode, and multi-column layouts
extras: The README explicitly recommends the rival plugin imshenshen/obsidian-sticky-heading for users who prefer a more minimalist display, since its default mode is equivalent to this plugin's concise mode.
intentEvidence: there's already a plugin with similar functionality in the Obsidian Plugin Market: Obsidian Sticky Heading
motivation: The author wanted to bring VS Code's Sticky Scroll feature to Obsidian and had wanted to do so for six months.
problem: Obsidian's outline sits in a separate pane, so while scrolling a long note you lose sight of which section you are in.

relations.evidence: The imshenshen/obsidian-sticky-heading plugin, by default, only displays the current heading
after seeing the Sticky Scroll feature in the VS Code editor, I found it incredibly useful

summary: Sticky heading bar that shows the current heading tree at the top of the pane while editing or reading, with click-to-jump navigation.
